choice: In zip recipe import, stopped reusing category and tag ids from the archive when creating missing ones, because an id that already belongs to another group's row would likely make the import fail.
final:
I changed one thing: zip recipe import no longer reuses category and tag ids from the archive. I didn't write a test that reproduces the old crash, so I haven't confirmed it happens.

The full `python3 -m pytest` run (with `-x`) shows only skips (LDAP, psycopg2, the long-running parser tests), no failures. I saw only the tail of the output.

I was looking for cross-group problems in `create_from_zip` (`mealie/services/recipe/recipe_service.py`). The recipe id, foods, units and nested instruction, ingredient and note ids were already handled. The gap was in `_transform_category_or_tag`. When an archive had a category or tag the group didn't have, it created the new row using the id from the archive. If that id already belonged to another group's row, the import would most likely fail with a database integrity error instead of creating the tag. The fix drops the incoming `id` before the create, so the database generates a fresh one.

CHOICE: In zip recipe import, stopped reusing category and tag ids from the archive when creating missing ones, because an id that already belongs to another group's row would likely make the import fail.
